topic.label: Quantum Physics
topic.desc: Quantum physics: foundations and measurement, wave mechanics, spin, quantum information, many-body physics, field theory, open systems and quantum optics.

concepts: Postulates, wavefunctions, measurement and the uncertainty principle.
Solving the Schrodinger equation exactly and approximately.
Angular momentum algebra, spin systems and the hydrogen atom.
Qubits, circuits, algorithms and error correction.
Systems of many quantum particles: bands, tensor networks and second quantization.
Fields, Feynman diagrams and the Standard Model.
Density matrices, master equations and decoherence.
skills: Explains the postulates, the Born rule and measurement outcomes with worked examples and states where interpretation begins.
Computes commutators and uncertainty bounds for observables and shows which pairs are compatible.
Compares interpretations of quantum mechanics side by side and labels what is experimentally distinguishable and what is not.
Solves the time-independent and time-dependent equation for wells, oscillators and barriers and reports energy levels and wavefunctions.
Applies perturbation theory and the variational principle and reports error bounds for the approximation.
Computes transmission, reflection and tunneling probabilities and scattering cross sections.
Adds angular momenta and builds Clebsch-Gordan coefficients and ladder-operator results.
Simulates spin one-half systems with Pauli matrices, the Bloch sphere and precession in a magnetic field.
Derives hydrogen energy levels and orbitals and the first fine-structure corrections.
Designs and simulates small qubit circuits with gates and noise models and returns measurement histograms.
Analyzes simple quantum error-correcting codes, their syndromes and the error types they correct.
Explains quantum algorithms and compares their resource counts with classical methods without claiming speedups that are not proven.
Computes tight-binding band structures and identifies gaps, effective masses and topological features.
Simulates one-dimensional lattice models with matrix product states and DMRG and reports entanglement and truncation error.
Writes many-particle Hamiltonians for fermions and bosons with creation and annihilation operators.
Draws diagrams and writes amplitudes for simple scattering processes at lowest order.
Explains the particles and forces of the Standard Model and which questions it leaves open.
Explains renormalization and running couplings and when a cutoff matters.
Builds density matrices for pure and mixed states and computes purity, entropy and partial traces.
Simulates open-system dynamics with Lindblad master equations and shows relaxation and dephasing.
Estimates decoherence times from coupling to an environment and relates them to the classical limit.
Analyzes coherent, thermal and squeezed light by photon-number statistics and correlation functions.
Outlines atom interferometer and clock measurements and their sensitivity limits and noise sources.
